interface.title: KAI - Calcium Imaging Analyzer (Streamlit app_streamlit.py)
interface.field: Cell physiology / cardiac electrophysiology: calcium-imaging transient analysis
interface.stage_of_work: Signal processing and analysis of recorded time series, from raw trace to curated metrics and an exported bundle
interface.what_it_is_for: Turn a raw periodic calcium-imaging trace (optionally ambient-subtracted) into curated beat-by-beat periods, a normalized mean ± SD overlay, and aggregated transient-morphology metrics (APD20/50/90, rise/decay, slopes, AUC), exported as XLSX, PNG and session JSON.

data.note: sample_raw_signal_data.csv (t,i, about 5 s and 5 transients) was uploaded through 'Load Raw...', and sample_ambient_signal_data.csv through 'Load Ambient (optional)...'. Subtracting the ambient moved the baseline from about 170 to about 3–5 a.u. (screens/009.webp). A second, fresh session used raw only (screens/054.webp).

tree.general: Quantify the shape of repeated transients in a periodic time-series recording and save a reproducible record of the analysis
tree.specific: Analyse a paced calcium-imaging trace in KAI: subtract ambient, set pacing, smooth, detect and curate periods, review overlay and APD/slope/AUC metrics, export XLSX/PNG/session.json

children.general: Read how the method works
children.specific: User Guide tab

children.general: Get the method documentation
children.specific: Open the User Guide tab, which covers S levels, APD definitions and the export sheets. A '⬇️ Download User-Guide.md' button is also shown but was not pressed

children.general: Bring in the recording and remove background
children.specific: Load Raw / Load Ambient and Ambient alignment in the sidebar

children.general: Load the primary time series
children.specific: Upload the raw calcium trace CSV; the Signal tab plots 'Raw' against Time (s)

children.general: Subtract a background recording from the signal
children.specific: Upload the ambient trace; the plot switches to an 'Ambient-corrected' trace with baseline near 3–5 a.u.

children.general: Adjust the time shift and gain of the background before subtracting it
children.specific: Set Offset (ms) and Scale under Ambient alignment and press Apply. Offset 20 ms with scale 0.9 left the baseline near 20 (under-subtracted), so it was set back to 0 / 1.0

children.label: typed Offset (ms) = 20 and Scale = 0.9, pressed Apply

children.general: Denoise and segment the trace into cycles
children.specific: Pacing (manual), the Smoothing S slider and Detect Peaks

children.general: Set the expected cycle rate so detection ignores peaks spaced too closely
children.specific: Enter Hz under Pacing (manual) and press Use; 'Current: auto' changes to 'Current: 1 Hz'. Pacing mainly sets Detect Peaks' minimum peak spacing (about 0.6 × the period); it changes the smoothing filter only at S≥3, through the Butterworth cutoff. Set it before smoothing and detection (in this run it was set after a first auto-pacing detection)

children.general: Choose a smoothing strength that removes noise but keeps transient shape
children.specific: Move the S = 0..5 slider; a 'Filtered (S=n)' trace is drawn over the corrected signal. With auto pacing, S=1 and S=3 barely changed the trace. With pacing at 1 Hz, S=3 flattened the peaks, so S=1 was kept

children.label: clicked slider track at S=1 (after setting 1 Hz pacing)

children.general: Automatically find peaks and troughs and split the trace into cycles
children.specific: Press Detect Peaks to mark max/min, draw numbered period boundaries and shade the incomplete edge regions red. Auto pacing at S=3 gave 13 periods, many of them spurious, because the estimated rate allowed closely spaced peaks. 1 Hz at S=3 gave 4. 1 Hz at S=1 gave 5 clean periods. Raw only at S=0 with auto pacing gave 9, including a 0.18 s period

children.label: pressed Detect Peaks on raw-only trace in a fresh session (S=0, auto)

children.general: Check the detected cycles' lengths for spurious short cycles
children.specific: The Periods tab lists 'Period NN: N=samples duration=s' (at 1 Hz, S=1: 0.645, 1.089, 0.931, 0.889, 0.952 s)

children.general: Curate which cycles count
children.specific: Edit Mode: click maxima and minima on the Signal plot. The plot redraws one click late, and clicks made while it redraws are ignored, so check the Periods list after each click and repeat a click that had no effect

children.general: Exclude an artifactual or incomplete cycle
children.specific: With Edit Mode on, click Period 1's maximum. Period 01 (0.645 s, out of phase in the overlay) drops from the list and is shaded red (the shading can appear only on the next redraw), and the overlay and metrics recompute on periods 2–5. Clicking the same maximum again, which the README says restores the period, did not restore it in this run (unconfirmed; possibly a click lost during a redraw)

children.label: clicked orange max marker of period 1 at t≈0.264 s

children.general: Remove a cycle boundary (merge two cycles)
children.specific: Click the minimum at t=3.776 s. Periods 4 and 5 merge into Period 04 of 1.851 s, and an overlay drawn on the Signal tab shows it as a double hump. A click made while the plot is still redrawing is ignored and has to be repeated

children.label: clicked blue min marker at t=3.776 s

children.general: Insert a missing cycle boundary
children.specific: Click the filtered trace in the trough at t≈3.78 s to add a minimum. The list goes back to Period 04 (0.889 s) and Period 05 (0.952 s), while the plot still shows the merged boundary until the next redraw. As with merging, a click during a redraw is ignored

children.general: Review consistency and measurements
children.specific: Overlay and Metrics tabs

children.general: Superimpose the kept cycles on a normalized time axis and check mean ± spread
children.specific: The Overlay tab plots each kept period against normalized time τ, with a mean line and SD band; the 'Normalized amplitude' axis runs to about 15, not 0–1. Use it with Edit Mode off: with Edit Mode on, the tab shows 'Overlay error: There are multiple plotly_chart elements with the same auto-generated ID'

children.general: Read aggregated shape metrics across kept cycles and check they are plausible
children.specific: The Metrics tab gives Raw mean/std and Filt mean/std for APD20, APD50, APD90, rise_10_90, decay_90_10, time_to_peak, up/downstroke angle, auc_above_baseline and min/max slopes. It updates after curation, e.g. APD20 0.1079 → 0.1087. Only aggregates are shown; per-period values are said to be in the XLSX but were not verified. Check APD ordering: in this run raw APD90 (0.053) came out below raw APD50 (0.208), the reversed-APD case the User Guide says to fix by lowering S, verifying the minima and re-detecting (not tried here)

children.general: Save results and a reproducibility record
children.specific: Export XLSX/CSV, then the download buttons

children.general: Export the workbook, figures and a session snapshot
children.specific: Export XLSX/CSV shows Download XLSX, Download signal.png, Download periods_overlay.png and Download session.json. Each download reruns the app and hides the buttons, so Export has to be pressed again before each file. session.json held smoothing_level 1, peaks_min/max indices, removed_periods [1], the ambient offset/scale/mean/std and n_periods 4 (these curated values come from this run only; the replay exported an uncurated session). The workbook's sheets (Parameters, Aggregates, per-period metrics, Resampled_Periods) and the PNGs' contents are unverified

features.name: Background-trace subtraction with time-offset and gain alignment
features.general: Load an optional reference/background series, shift it in time and scale it, subtract it from the main signal, and see the corrected trace right away
features.specific: Load Ambient (optional) plus Ambient alignment: Offset (ms), Scale, Apply. The Signal plot switches to 'Ambient-corrected'
steps: Upload the background file next to the main signal
Check the corrected trace's baseline
Enter a time offset and a scale factor
Press Apply and compare the baseline; repeat until it sits at the expected level
serves_tasks: Subtract a background recording from the signal
Adjust the time shift and gain of the background before subtracting it

features.name: Single-dial smoothing with a live filtered overlay
features.general: One 0–5 strength dial for a low-pass filter, with the filtered trace drawn over the unfiltered one; at the strongest levels the cutoff follows the expected cycle rate
features.specific: S = 0..5 slider and the 'Filtered (S=n)' overlay on the Signal plot; at S≥3 the Butterworth cutoff depends on the pacing rate ('Current: auto' or '1 Hz')
steps: Move the S slider (keyboard or click on the track; dragging did not work)
Compare the Filtered trace with the corrected trace for flattened peaks
Lower S if peaks are rounded
serves_tasks: Choose a smoothing strength that removes noise but keeps transient shape

features.name: Rate-aware peak/trough detection with numbered cycle segmentation
features.general: Use a user-given or estimated cycle rate to set the minimum spacing between peaks, find maxima and minima, split the series into numbered min-to-min cycles, mark incomplete edge cycles as excluded, and list each cycle's sample count and duration
features.specific: Pacing (manual) Hz + Use sets the minimum peak distance (about 0.6 × period); Detect Peaks then puts orange max and blue min markers on the plot, dashed boundaries with period numbers, red-shaded edge regions, and the Periods tab list
steps: Enter the pacing rate and press Use (otherwise it is estimated)
Press Detect Peaks
Inspect the markers and numbered periods on the plot
Check the durations in the Periods tab
If there are spurious short periods, set the pacing or change S and re-detect
serves_tasks: Set the expected cycle rate so detection ignores peaks spaced too closely
Automatically find peaks and troughs and split the trace into cycles
Check the detected cycles' lengths for spurious short cycles

features.name: Click-to-curate cycles on a time-series plot
features.general: In an edit mode, click a cycle's peak to exclude it, click a trough marker to delete a boundary, or click the trace to insert one; all downstream summaries recompute
features.specific: Edit Mode checkbox plus clicks on the Signal plot: max toggles the period (red shading, dropped from the Periods list; restoring by a second click was not confirmed), a min click removes a boundary, a trace click adds a minimum. The plot redraws one click late and ignores clicks made during a redraw
steps: Tick Edit Mode
Click a maximum to exclude that period (a second click should restore it; unconfirmed)
Click a minimum marker to merge neighbouring periods
Click the trace at a trough to insert a boundary
After each click, wait for the redraw and check the Periods list and metrics; repeat a click that had no effect
Turn Edit Mode off before opening the Overlay tab
serves_tasks: Exclude an artifactual or incomplete cycle
Remove a cycle boundary (merge two cycles)

features.name: Normalized cycle overlay with mean ± SD band
features.general: Rescale each kept cycle to a common 0–1 time axis, overlay them, and draw the mean with a dispersion band so outlier cycles stand out
features.specific: Overlay tab: 'Normalized time τ' vs 'Normalized amplitude' (axis runs to about 15), Period n traces, a Mean line and an SD band, updated by curation. With Edit Mode on, the Overlay tab errors ('multiple plotly_chart elements with the same auto-generated ID'); an overlay is then drawn on the Signal tab instead
steps: Detect periods
Turn Edit Mode off and open Overlay
Spot traces out of phase with the mean (e.g. short Period 1, or a merged double hump)
Go back and curate, then re-check the band
serves_tasks: Superimpose the kept cycles on a normalized time axis and check mean ± spread
Exclude an artifactual or incomplete cycle

features.name: Aggregated transient-morphology metrics table (raw vs filtered)
features.general: Compute per-cycle shape metrics (durations to 20/50/90% recovery, rise and decay times, time to peak, slopes, area) and show the mean and SD across kept cycles for both the unsmoothed and the smoothed signal
features.specific: Metrics tab: APD20/50/90, rise_10_90, decay_90_10, time_to_peak, up/downstroke angle, auc_above_baseline, min/max slope, with Raw mean, Raw std, Filt mean and Filt std columns. Only aggregates are shown in the UI
steps: Detect and curate periods
Open Metrics
Check that APD20 < APD50 < APD90; if reversed, lower S, verify the minima and re-detect
Compare the Raw and Filt columns to judge how smoothing affects each metric
Re-check after excluding periods
serves_tasks: Read aggregated shape metrics across kept cycles and check they are plausible

features.name: Export bundle with session snapshot
features.general: Generate a workbook, figure images and a JSON record of parameters and curation decisions in one step, then download each
features.specific: Export XLSX/CSV, then Download XLSX (output.xlsx), signal.png, periods_overlay.png and session.json (smoothing_level, peaks_min/max, removed_periods, meta_ambient, n_periods; manual pacing Hz is not recorded). Workbook sheet contents unverified
steps: Finish curation
Press Export XLSX/CSV
Download each file (press Export again after each download, because the buttons disappear)
Keep session.json with the data, and note the pacing Hz separately
serves_tasks: Export the workbook, figures and a session snapshot
